case.description: TEST-ONLY: a factory table by bends crossed.

location.text: hole 1 to hole 2, midway, at x 2.125, y 12.5, z 7.875

findings.message: passes: hole 1 to hole 2 crosses 1 bend. This shop's table gives plus or minus 0.2 mm there, within the plus or minus 0.3 mm needed. This says nothing about anything but this dimension.

requirement.text: At least 0.2 mm. TEST-ONLY: a distance.

location.text: hole 1 to hole 2, midway, at x 2.125, y 12.5, z 7.875

findings.message: too tight: hole 1 to hole 2 crosses 1 bend. This shop's table gives plus or minus 0.2 mm there, and this needs plus or minus 0.15 mm. Put both holes on one flat, have them cut after bending, or allow plus or minus 0.2 mm.
needs: A person to choose: move a hole, have them cut after bending, or loosen the tolerance.

requirement.text: At least 0.2 mm. TEST-ONLY: a distance.

findings.message: one hole: both points are at hole 1, so there's no dimension to check.
needs: For one hole, two points at two different round holes.

findings.message: nowhere: no round hole this version can measure is within 1 mm of one of its points, beyond half the sheet's thickness.
needs: For nowhere, points within 1 mm of two round holes' centres. A report's part.holes lists them; only holes square to the skins and through the sheet count.

bends_gate.message: 2 bends found. Every face has a label, and skins that aren't in one plane join only through bends. This only says the bends were found.

exceptions: A punching figure used as a floor for every process, so it can only warn.
requirements.method: The most lenient published value we may use. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.
requirements.rights: Unclear. One published figure, restated with its source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.
requirements.source: Mate Precision Technologies, punching: 0.5t, its lowest figure, for fully guided tooling in aluminium. Used for every process and material, so it assumes nothing about this part: https://www.mate.com/technical-resources/punch-press-resources/tips-techniques/punching/techniques/holes/

exceptions: Published values differ by more than six times, and the source doesn't say which process it means.
requirements.measuring_line: The hole's edge to the nearest cut edge on the same flat.
requirements.method: The most lenient published value we may use. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.
requirements.rights: Unclear. One published figure, restated with its source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.
requirements.source: Five Flute, sheet metal DFM design guidelines: https://www.fiveflute.com/guide/sheet-metal-dfm-design-guidelines-for-formed-and-punched-parts

exceptions: Worded as a risk: the file can't say whether a hole is cut after bending.
requirements.measuring_line: 2.5t + r, a labelled trial value: the hole's edge to the nearest bend tangent on the same flat.
requirements.method: A labelled trial value. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.
requirements.rights: Unclear. One published figure, restated with its source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.
requirements.source: PTC Creo design rules default, also in Five Flute and Fictiv, which probably share one origin: https://support.ptc.com/help/creo/creo_pma/r7.0/usascii/sheetmetal/sheetmetaldesign/Set_Up/About_Design_Rules.html

exceptions: Geomiq's depth figure, 0.6 mm below the material thickness, was read again on 2026-11-10 and is still unclear in what it measures, so it isn't used.
requirements.measuring_line: The countersink's depth, from the skin to where the cone meets the hole's wall.
requirements.method: The most lenient published value we may use. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.
requirements.rights: Unclear. One published figure, restated with its source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.
requirements.source: PCBWay, countersink and counterbore design guidelines: at most 0.70t. Fictiv's 60 to 70% agrees at its top end: https://www.pcbway.com/blog/Sheet_Metal/Countersink_Counterbore_Holes_Design_Guidelines_f328f60a.html

exceptions: PCBWay's centre to edge of twice the major diameter is stricter whenever d is more than 2t.
requirements.measuring_line: The countersink's rim to the nearest cut edge on the same flat. Another countersink's rim counts as a cut edge.
requirements.method: The most lenient published value we may use. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.
requirements.rights: Unclear. One published figure, restated with its source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.
requirements.source: Geomiq, sheet metal design guide: 4t from an edge to the countersink's centre, moved to the rim by taking off half the major diameter d. Xometry also gives 4t: https://geomiq.com/sheet-metal-design-guide/

exceptions: If Geomiq's bend line is the bend's centreline, the published value is lower than this by half the bend allowance, which r and t can't write exactly.
requirements.measuring_line: The countersink's rim to the nearest bend tangent on the same flat.
requirements.method: The most lenient published value we may use. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.
requirements.rights: Unclear. One published figure, restated with its source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.
requirements.source: Geomiq, sheet metal design guide: 3t from the bend line to the countersink's centre, moved to the rim. Its bend line is read as the bend's tangent, an assumption. Xometry also gives 3t: https://geomiq.com/sheet-metal-design-guide/

exceptions: Mate also gives 2t. A lower laser figure from one shop's own specification is left out.
requirements.measuring_line: The wall between two round holes on the same flat, edge to edge.
requirements.method: The most lenient published value we may use. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.
requirements.rights: Unclear. One published figure, restated with its source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.
requirements.source: Five Flute, sheet metal DFM design guidelines, the publisher of the hole-to-edge row: https://www.fiveflute.com/guide/sheet-metal-dfm-design-guidelines-for-formed-and-punched-parts

thickness_gate.message: The model's sheet matches the declared 1.5 mm within 0.02 mm, a placeholder. This only says it matches what was declared. It doesn't confirm that value is the real gauge.
